When Freaky Birds Nearly Attack

Jun 3, 2009 • Janice Cotcher

About eight years ago as I arrived at my parents’ house, my headlights shone on this bird waddling across the driveway: [!]American bittern on a driveway

Don’t let appearance deceive you, the bird on the driveway way about 2 feet tall and its beak was about 5 inches long. It was the strangest looking thing I had ever seen in my entire life*. I walked into the house, said nothing to my family and grab my brother by the arm and pulled him outside; I needed someone else to witness it and I was too flabbergasted for words. My brother has no idea what was going on until he saw the bird. I grabbed my camera and we followed it to the neighbour’s semi-enclosed patio. After taking a couple pictures, the bird started aggressively squawking and started walking toward us. My brother shouted “Let’s get out of here! I don’t want to be part of a new Fox special ‘When Freaky Birds Attack’!”**

For years, I’ve been asking people what type of bird this might be. I misplaced the pictures on one of my moves so it didn’t help the situation. Today in class we had a presentation by a naturalist on the biodiversity in Wascana Park and I found out it was an American Bittern! After his presentation, I told the naturalist about my experience and he was surprised the bird was so far from the marsh. Their beaks are used for catching fish but is also used to defend itself against hawks and eagles. It was probably either hurt or confused so it was a good thing we kept our distance.

*Still trumps the goat jumping on the llamas back. ** It amazing me the things my brother thinks of on the fly. Growing up, sitting beside him in church was a huge distraction. —
